issues.description: In the reference solution, the REST endpoint handler PersonResource.createPerson is declared as "protected", while the other endpoint methods in the same class are "public". In Spring MVC controller classes, endpoint handler methods are typically public; the mixed visibility is inconsistent and can confuse students about what visibility they should use when implementing the endpoint in the template.
issues.suggestedFix: Change PersonResource.createPerson in the solution to "public" for consistency with the other endpoint methods and typical Spring controller conventions.

issues.description: The problem statement uses the term "Edit" for the client-side update operation in the referenced test names (e.g., "Edit single person"), but the method students must implement is named updatePerson in both the template and solution. This terminology mismatch can make it harder to map the task description/tests to the actual method to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Adjust the problem statement wording/test labels in Part 2 to consistently refer to the client method name "updatePerson" when describing the update/edit operation.
